children.note: Log parameters, metrics, artifacts, and tags across training runs; organize with experiments; compare runs in notebook UI (Delta/UC backend).
Automatic capture from scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, PyTorch, LightGBM; configurable via mlflow.autolog(); requires explicit enabling on serverless compute.
Web interface for managing experiments, comparing runs across metrics/artifacts, inspecting nested traces from agent/LLM calls.
First-class model entities with versioning, signature inference, metrics, parameters, and lineage tracking across training/staging/prod.
8 built-in judges (correctness, relevance, safety, groundedness, completeness, fluency, tool-call quality, RAG sufficiency) + human feedback loops.
Define Python evaluation logic using @scorer decorator; deterministic checks, custom metrics, or domain-specific heuristics without LLM overhead.
Version prompts with immutable history; stage aliases (champion/staging/prod) for promotion workflows; bind model params and temperature together.
Capture end-to-end agent execution: prompts, model calls, retrievals, tool invocations, errors, latency; OpenTelemetry-compatible for debugging/monitoring.
Binary & multiclass prediction via decision trees, random forests, logistic regression, XGBoost, LightGBM; stratified train/val/test splits (60/20/20).
Continuous value prediction via trees, linear regression, XGBoost, LightGBM with automated hyperparameter tuning and evaluation metrics (R², MAE, RMSE).
Time-series predictions via Prophet or Auto-ARIMA on classic Databricks clusters; configurable forecast horizon, external regressors via Feature Store.
Prophet, Auto-ARIMA, and DeepAR on managed serverless GPU infrastructure; no cluster provisioning required.
Editable trial code for every model trained; inspect data exploration, preprocessing, feature engineering, training logic, SHAP analysis; reproducible and customizable.
Feature importance and impact analysis via SHAP Shapley values; disabled by default (memory-intensive); enable with shap_enabled=True in notebooks.
Automatic semantic type detection, missing-value imputation, column inclusion/exclusion, categorical encoding; supported types: numeric, categorical, text, dates, arrays.
Programmatic interface (databricks.automl.classify/regress/forecast) with full control: exclude_cols, imputers, time_col, split_col, feature_store_lookups.

since: GA (AI Runtime: Jun 2026 PuP; ML Runtime: foundational)

children.note: Cluster runtime with PyTorch (2.12.0), scikit-learn (1.7.2), XGBoost (3.2.0), TensorFlow (legacy on Runtime 17.3 LTS only), GPU drivers; Spark MLlib support.
Managed serverless GPU compute: 1×A10 (24 GB), 1×H100 (80 GB), or 8×H100 (per GPU). Pay-per-minute, scale-to-zero. Notebook and CLI access. Public Preview status Oct 2026.
Framework-agnostic distributed training orchestration; multi-GPU/multi-node support for PyTorch, TensorFlow; integrates with Ray Data and Ray Tune for end-to-end pipelines.
Distributed parallel hyperparameter trials with ASHA early stopping; per-trial GPU reservations; integrates with MLflow for experiment tracking and child-run logging.
Launcher for distributed PyTorch via Spark cluster resources; wraps torch.distributed.run; minimal migration from existing DDP code; Spark 3.4+ / Runtime 13.0 ML+.
Distributed classification, regression, clustering, collaborative filtering; pyspark.ml API for scalable ML on massive datasets; dimensionality reduction and feature engineering.
ZeRO sharding (stages 1-3), optimizer/gradient partitioning, CPU offload; via TorchDistributor on classic compute or AI Runtime; Llama 2 7B fine-tuning examples provided.
Notebook decorator for single-node multi-GPU training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed); serverless execution on AI Runtime; replaces TorchDistributor for compatible workloads without Spark.
